findings.at: ### Reversibility — 'Overturn: C-D174. Does not unwrite D-013, D-104, D-106, D-161, D-169, D-172, or D-173.'
findings.charge: The Reversibility clause omits D-170 and D-171 from its non-unwrite enumeration, breaking a convention applied without exception by the five preceding entries, and contradicting this same draft's own Decision-type line, which names D-170 and D-171 as members of the branch this entry continues.
evidence: The convention across the wave is row-specific history plus the contiguous chain of decisions from D-169 to the immediately preceding entry. D-169: 'D-032, D-129, D-164, D-167, or D-168'. D-170: 'D-032, D-164, D-167, D-168, or D-169'. D-171: 'D-032, D-042, D-163, D-169, or D-170'. D-172: 'D-086, D-169, D-170, or D-171'. D-173: 'D-114, D-160, D-169, D-170, D-171, or D-172'. Each covers the contiguous span with no gap.

D-174 lists 'D-013, D-104, D-106, D-161, D-169, D-172, or D-173'. The DR-103 row history (D-013, D-104, D-106, D-161) is correct and complete, but the contiguous span from D-169 to D-173 is broken: D-170 and D-171 are absent.

The omission has no principled basis. D-172 (exact-bytes / G07) and D-173 (distribution-core / DR-101) are included even though neither bears on DR-103, while D-170 (doctor-actor / DR-114) and D-171 (permission / DR-105) are excluded despite being structurally identical acts — leftover-join recordings on the same no-cell-edit branch. The immediate precedent D-172 included D-170 and D-171 for exactly this reason.

The draft contradicts itself: its Decision-type block states 'Same no-cell-edit branch as D-170 / D-171 / D-172 / D-173', naming all four, and the Reversibility clause then preserves only two of them. D-170 and D-171 are the only two decisions in the D-169-through-D-173 span that appear in one clause and not the other.

Both omitted decisions are live and unqualified: D-170 and D-171 each carry Status ADOPTED 2026-08-20, and the only C-D170 / C-D171 occurrences in COORD are their own Overturn labels and Commit lines — no overturn has been executed against either. So neither is excluded because its standing had lapsed.
The review instruction for this turn is 'Do not unwrite D-169 through D-173' — the full span. The entry's operative clause affirmatively preserves only part of the span it was instructed to preserve.
findings.whyThisMatters: The Reversibility clause is the operative record of what survives an overturn via C-D174, and after adoption it becomes permanent history that a later auditor executing C-D174 will read to determine what stays written. Leaving D-170 and D-171 unnamed makes their standing under C-D174 unstated at exactly the moment the entry becomes immutable. This is turn 1 of 3 and the clause is one line, so the cost of completing it now is negligible against the cost of a permanent gap.
findings.whyNotAMustFix: Omission from a protective enumeration is not an unwrite. The entry performs no edit, makes no false claim about D-170 or D-171, and its header independently forbids any COORD change beyond the append-only adoption of this entry. Nothing in the draft endangers either decision; the defect is incompleteness in a scope declaration, not a prohibited act.
findings.suggestedRepairShape: Restore the contiguous span in the Reversibility clause: 'Does not unwrite D-013, D-104, D-106, D-161, D-169, D-170, D-171, D-172, or D-173.' This is a one-line addition that touches no digest, no pin, no measured input, and no other clause, and it brings the entry into agreement with both the D-169-through-D-173 convention and its own Decision-type line.
findings.notARequestTo: This finding does not ask for any change to the recording of v6, to the DR-103 standing, to required-now 28, to the five protected leftover-design obligations, to file 08, or to the Stage A evidence. It does not ask for D-170 or D-171 to be reopened, re-recorded, or otherwise disturbed.
